Runs standard OCI containers. |+| `KataVmIsolation` | Enables pod sandboxing with Kata Containers alongside standard OCI containers. Pods that specify `runtimeClassName: kata-vm-isolation` run in lightweight VMs with their own guest kernel. |++Setting `workloadRuntime: KataVmIsolation` doesn't sandbox every pod on the node. Pods that don't request the Kata runtime continue to run as standard containers and can share the same node.++### Pod sandboxing requirements++- Set `imageFamily: AzureLinux`. Karpenter automatically filters for compatible sizes and selects the Kata-enabled Azure Linux image. If you constrain VM sizes in a `NodePool`, leave compatible sizes available.+- Don't set `fipsMode: FIPS` or enable Trusted Launch. The managed cluster must run Kubernetes version 1.35 or later.+- You must create the resource group for the workload space in West Central US (`westcentralus`).+- Ensure that your subscription has sufficient AKS, ACI, and networking quota for the selected region.+- Ensure that you have permission to create resources and register resource providers and preview features. A subscription administrator with directory read access must approve and assign the application roles described in this procedure.+- To capture and restore workload state, also meet the requirements for the optional [Pod snapshot cluster extension (preview)](pod-snapshot-cluster-extension).+- Install Azure CLI version 2.85.0 or later, PowerShell 7 or later, and `kubectl`. Run `az --version` to find your CLI version and `az upgrade` to upgrade. Run all commands for the selected path in the same PowerShell session. For more information, see [Install Azure CLI](/en-us/cli/azure/install-azure-cli).+- Install [kubelogin](kubelogin-authentication) for Microsoft Entra authentication to the managed AKS cluster.++## Limitations++- The serverless sandbox runtime is available in Central US, North Central US, West US 2, East US 2, Australia East, Sweden Central, and West Central US.+- Container images must come from Microsoft Container Registry (`mcr.microsoft.com`) or Azure Container Registry (`*.azurecr.io`). Direct pulls from other registries, including Docker Hub, are rejected by this preview runtime.+- AKS Automatic isn't yet supported.++## Prepare the Workload Manager environment++The following steps create billable Azure resources. Use a dedicated resource group and keep the deployment values unchanged throughout provisioning.++1. Install or update the Workload Manager CLI extension to preview version `1.0.0b1`.++    ```powershell+    az extension add --name workload-manager --version 1.0.0b1 `+      --allow-preview true --upgrade+    ```++    Verify the installed version.++    ```powershell+    az extension show --name workload-manager --query version --output tsv+    ```+2. Set your subscription ID, resource group name, and workload space name. The workload space name must contain 3 to 16 lowercase letters or digits.++    ```powershell+    $SUBSCRIPTION_ID = "<subscription-id>"+    $RESOURCE_GROUP = "<new-resource-group-name>"+    $SPACE_NAME = "<workload-space-name>"+    $LOCATION = "<supported-region>"+    $SUBSCRIPTION_SCOPE = "/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID"+    $RESOURCE_GROUP_SCOPE = "$SUBSCRIPTION_SCOPE/resourceGroups/$RESOURCE_GROUP"+    $WORKLOAD_SPACE_ID = "$RESOURCE_GROUP_SCOPE/providers/Microsoft.Compute/workloadSpaces/$SPACE_NAME"+    $AKS_BINDING_NAME = "$SPACE_NAME-aks"+    $ACI_BINDING_NAME = "$SPACE_NAME-aci"+    $LINK_NAME = "$SPACE_NAME-link"+    $AKS_BINDING_ID = "$WORKLOAD_SPACE_ID/runtimeBindings/$AKS_BINDING_NAME"+    $ACI_BINDING_ID = "$WORKLOAD_SPACE_ID/runtimeBindings/$ACI_BINDING_NAME"+    ```+3. Register and select a regional ARM cloud profile. This profile routes ARM requests to `https://westcentralus.management.azure.com/`. Azure CLI discovers the other endpoints automatically. If the profile is already registered, skip the registration command and select it.++    ```powershell+    az cloud register `+      --name WorkloadRP-WestCentralUS `+      --endpoint-resource-manager "https://westcentralus.management.azure.com/"+    ```++    ```powershell+    az cloud set --name WorkloadRP-WestCentralUS+    ```+4. Sign in to the selected cloud and set your subscription before registering features, assigning roles, or creating resources. Sign in again after changing cloud profiles; an existing AzureCloud session doesn't replace this step.++    The `--subscription` option for `az login` requires Azure CLI 2.85.0 or later, as specified in the prerequisites.++    ```powershell+    az login --subscription "$SUBSCRIPTION_ID"+    ```+5. Register the preview feature if it isn't already registered, and check its registration status.++    ```powershell+    az feature register --namespace Microsoft.Compute --name WorkloadManagerPreview+    ```++    ```powershell+    az feature show --namespace Microsoft.Compute `+      --name WorkloadManagerPreview --query properties.state --output tsv+    ```++    Repeat the `show` command until it returns `Registered`. Don't continue until registration is complete.+6. Create the resource group for the workload space and its managed resources.++    ```powershell+    az group create --name "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --location westcentralus+    ```+7. Register the required resource providers.++    ```powershell+    az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Compute --wait+    az provider register --namespace Microsoft.ContainerService --wait+    az provider register --namespace Microsoft.ContainerInstance --wait+    az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Network --wait+    az provider register --namespace Microsoft.ManagedIdentity --wait+    az provider register --namespace Microsoft.KubernetesConfiguration --wait+    ```++## Authorize the Workload Manager application++A subscription administrator must grant the Workload Manager application (`032854b2-ba65-4dd6-bdd4-4e86b8756667`) the following roles at the resource group scope. Azure CLI resolves the application to its service principal in the tenant you're signed in to.++Before assigning permissions to either application in this procedure, record any existing role assignments. For each newly created assignment, save the `id` returned by Azure CLI for cleanup. Don't remove preexisting or shared assignments during cleanup.++A repeated create command can return an existing assignment. Don't treat its returned ID as a newly created assignment.++The `--assignee` option requires a Microsoft Graph lookup. If token-protection Conditional Access blocks Microsoft Graph authentication, ask a directory administrator for each application's tenant-specific service principal **Object ID** from **Enterprise applications** in the Microsoft Entra admin center. This isn't the application ID shown above. Use `--assignee-object-id` together with `--assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal` to avoid the Graph lookup without changing the required Azure permissions.++For example, use the following alternative for the Workload Manager Contributor grant. Use the same two assignee options for its other grants, preserving each role, scope, and condition.++```powershell+az role assignment create `+  --assignee-object-id "<workload-manager-service-principal-object-id>" `+  --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `+  --role "Contributor" `+  --scope "$RESOURCE_GROUP_SCOPE"+```++| Role | Purpose |+| --- | --- |+| **Contributor** | Creates and manages the Azure infrastructure. |+| **Role Based Access Control Administrator** | Creates and deletes role assignments, subject to the condition below. |+| **Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin** | Configures Kubernetes resources on the managed cluster. |++1. Grant **Contributor** and **Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin** at the resource group scope.++    ```powershell+    az role assignment create `+      --assignee "032854b2-ba65-4dd6-bdd4-4e86b8756667" `+      --role "Contributor" `+      --scope "$RESOURCE_GROUP_SCOPE"++    az role assignment create `+      --assignee "032854b2-ba65-4dd6-bdd4-4e86b8756667" `+      --role "Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin" `+      --scope "$RESOURCE_GROUP_SCOPE"+    ```+2. Define a condition that restricts write and delete operations on role assignments to service principals, including managed identities, and to these roles: Contributor, Network Contributor, and Azure Kubernetes Service Cluster Admin Role.++    Normalize the condition to a single line before passing it to Azure CLI.++    ```powershell+    $ROLE_CONDITION = @'+    (+      !(ActionMatches{'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'})+      OR (+        @Request[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:RoleDefinitionId] ForAnyOfAnyValues:GuidEquals {b24988ac-6180-42a0-ab88-20f7382dd24c, 4d97b98b-1d4f-4787-a291-c67834d212e7, 0ab0b1a8-8aac-4efd-b8c2-3ee1fb270be8}+        AND @Request[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:PrincipalType] ForAnyOfAnyValues:StringEqualsIgnoreCase {'ServicePrincipal'}+      )+    ) AND (+      !(ActionMatches{'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/delete'})+      OR (+        @Resource[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:RoleDefinitionId] ForAnyOfAnyValues:GuidEquals {b24988ac-6180-42a0-ab88-20f7382dd24c, 4d97b98b-1d4f-4787-a291-c67834d212e7, 0ab0b1a8-8aac-4efd-b8c2-3ee1fb270be8}+        AND @Resource[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:PrincipalType] ForAnyOfAnyValues:StringEqualsIgnoreCase {'ServicePrincipal'}+      )+    )+    '@+    $ROLE_CONDITION = ($ROLE_CONDITION -replace '[\r\n]+', ' ').Trim()+    ```+3. Assign **Role Based Access Control Administrator** with that condition.++    ```powershell+    az role assignment create `+      --assignee "032854b2-ba65-4dd6-bdd4-4e86b8756667" `+      --role "Role Based Access Control Administrator" `+      --scope "$RESOURCE_GROUP_SCOPE" `+      --condition "$ROLE_CONDITION" `+      --condition-version 2.0+    ```++    The condition limits this role assignment only. It doesn't restrict permissions granted through other assignments.++## Authorize the Compute Sandbox Groups application++For this preview, grant the **Compute Sandbox Groups** service principal (application ID `1eeacc2b-ec4a-4b1e-977a-2b5fef2131c6`) the **Contributor**, **Azure Deployment Stack Owner**, and **Storage Blob Data Contributor** roles at the subscription scope. These roles allow the service to provision the managed resource group and snapshot storage account in your subscription. To assign the roles, you need permission to create role assignments on the subscription, such as the **Owner** or **User Access Administrator** role.++Warning++Have your subscription administrator review and approve these subscription-wide grants before continuing. The resource-group condition assigned to Workload Manager doesn't limit this application's access.++1. As an authorized administrator, assign the three roles.++    ```powershell+    $SANDBOX_ROLES = @(+      "Contributor"+      "Azure Deployment Stack Owner"+      "Storage Blob Data Contributor"+    )++    foreach ($ROLE in $SANDBOX_ROLES) {+      az role assignment create `+        --assignee "1eeacc2b-ec4a-4b1e-977a-2b5fef2131c6" `+        --role "$ROLE" `+        --scope "$SUBSCRIPTION_SCOPE"+    }+    ```++    If Microsoft Graph authentication is blocked, replace the `az role assignment create` command inside the loop with this alternative. Use the Compute Sandbox Groups service principal's tenant-specific Object ID, not its application ID.++    ```powershell+    az role assignment create `+      --assignee-object-id "<compute-sandbox-groups-service-principal-object-id>" `+      --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal `+      --role "$ROLE" `+      --scope "$SUBSCRIPTION_SCOPE"+    ```+2. Allow time for both applications' role assignments to propagate before creating the workload space and runtimes.++## Create the workload space and bindings++Create the resources in the following order. Provisioning the AKS and ACI bindings can take several minutes. For each binding and link, repeat its `show` command until `provisioningState` is `Succeeded` before continuing. Each binding must also have a nonempty `providerResourceId`.++The Workload Manager CLI extension version `1.0.0b1` doesn't expose a separate readiness `state` in its `show` output. Provisioning success alone doesn't verify that workloads can run. Complete the controller and runtime checks in the following list before deploying workloads.++1. Create the workload space, which manages the lifecycle of the runtime composition.++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space create `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --location "$LOCATION"+    ```++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space show `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --name "$SPACE_NAME"+    ```++    Wait for the parent resource's `provisioningState` to be `Succeeded` before creating the bindings.+2. Create the managed AKS binding with the `Standard` offering.++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space runtime-binding create `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --name "$AKS_BINDING_NAME" `+      --location "$LOCATION" `+      --kind Kubernetes `+      --managed '{managed-profile:{offering:Standard}}'+    ```++    Check the AKS binding.++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space runtime-binding show `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --name "$AKS_BINDING_NAME"+    ```+3. Create the managed ACI binding for the serverless sandbox runtime.++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space runtime-binding create `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --name "$ACI_BINDING_NAME" `+      --location "$LOCATION" `+      --kind ServerlessContainers `+      --managed '{managed-profile:{provider:ACI}}'+    ```++    Check the ACI binding.++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space runtime-binding show `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --name "$ACI_BINDING_NAME"+    ```+4. Check the underlying AKS and ACI resources before creating the runtime link. A binding can report `Succeeded` before its provider resource is ready.++    ```powershell+    foreach ($BINDING_NAME in @($AKS_BINDING_NAME, $ACI_BINDING_NAME)) {+      $PROVIDER_RESOURCE_ID = az workload-manager workload-space runtime-binding show `+        --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+        --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+        --name "$BINDING_NAME" `+        --query properties.providerResourceId --output tsv++      if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or+          [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($PROVIDER_RESOURCE_ID)) {+        throw "Couldn't resolve the provider resource for $BINDING_NAME."+      }++      az resource show --ids "$PROVIDER_RESOURCE_ID" `+        --query '{name:name,state:properties.provisioningState}'+    }+    ```++    Repeat the checks until both resources report `Succeeded`. If either resource reports `Failed`, resolve its provisioning error before continuing.+5. Link the AKS orchestrator to the serverless sandbox runtime by using the bindings' full resource IDs.++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space runtime-link create `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --name "$LINK_NAME" `+      --location "$LOCATION" `+      --orchestrator-binding "$AKS_BINDING_ID" `+      --execution-binding "$ACI_BINDING_ID"+    ```++    If creation returns `ProviderNotReady`, repeat the provider-resource checks, allow time for readiness to propagate, and retry the same create command. Don't recreate the workload space or bindings. Check that the runtime link reaches `Succeeded` before enabling Agent Sandbox.++    ```powershell+    az workload-manager workload-space runtime-link show `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --name "$LINK_NAME"+    ```+6. Resolve the managed AKS cluster for the controller and workload checks.++    ```powershell+    $AKS_RESOURCE_ID = az workload-manager workload-space runtime-binding show `+      --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --space-name "$SPACE_NAME" `+      --name "$AKS_BINDING_NAME" `+      --query properties.providerResourceId `+      --output tsv++    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($AKS_RESOURCE_ID)) {+      throw "The AKS binding hasn't returned a providerResourceId. Wait for provisioning to complete and try again."+    }+    ```++    ```powershell+    $AKS_RESOURCE_PARTS = $AKS_RESOURCE_ID.Trim('/').Split('/')+    if ($AKS_RESOURCE_PARTS.Length -ne 8 -or+        $AKS_RESOURCE_PARTS[2] -ne 'resourceGroups' -or+        $AKS_RESOURCE_PARTS[5] -ne 'Microsoft.ContainerService' -or+        $AKS_RESOURCE_PARTS[6] -ne 'managedClusters') {+      throw "The AKS binding hasn't returned a managed cluster resource ID."+    }++    $AKS_CLUSTER = az aks show `+      --resource-group "$($AKS_RESOURCE_PARTS[3])" `+      --name "$($AKS_RESOURCE_PARTS[7])" `+      --query '{name:name,resourceGroup:resourceGroup,kubernetesVersion:kubernetesVersion}' `+      --output json | ConvertFrom-Json++    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $null -eq $AKS_CLUSTER) {+      throw "Couldn't read the managed AKS cluster. Check binding provisioning and your access."+    }++    $CLUSTER_NAME = $AKS_CLUSTER.name+    $AKS_RESOURCE_GROUP = $AKS_CLUSTER.resourceGroup+    $AKS_CLUSTER+    ```++    Confirm that `kubernetesVersion` is 1.35 or later. Keep `RESOURCE_GROUP` unchanged: it identifies the workload space's resource group, which can differ from `AKS_RESOURCE_GROUP`.+7. Grant the walkthrough user Kubernetes administrator access if they don't already have it. Workload Manager's application role assignments don't grant your account access to Kubernetes resources. For a cluster that uses Azure RBAC, an authorized administrator can assign **Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin** at the cluster scope. These commands assign the role to the signed-in user.++    If Microsoft Graph authentication is blocked, replace the `az ad signed-in-user show` assignment with `$USER_OBJECT_ID = "<user-object-id>"`, using the user Object ID supplied by your directory administrator.++    ```powershell+    $USER_OBJECT_ID = az ad signed-in-user show --query id --output tsv+    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or+        [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($USER_OBJECT_ID)) {+      throw "Couldn't resolve the signed-in user."+    }++    az role assignment create `+      --assignee-object-id "$USER_OBJECT_ID" `+      --assignee-principal-type User `+      --role "Azure Kubernetes Service RBAC Cluster Admin" `+      --scope "$AKS_RESOURCE_ID"+    ```++    Record the assignment ID if you create it for this walkthrough. Allow time for role propagation before running Kubernetes commands. Getting cluster credentials alone doesn't grant Kubernetes access.++## Enable Agent Sandbox through the cluster extension++Install the extension directly on the AKS cluster. Use Agent Sandbox extension version `1.0.7` or later. The create command doesn't pin a version and uses the service-offered version with automatic upgrades enabled by default.++1. Install or update the cluster extension CLI.++    ```powershell+    az extension add --name k8s-extension --upgrade+    ```+2. Create the extension on the managed AKS cluster.++    ```powershell+    az k8s-extension create `+      --resource-group "$AKS_RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --cluster-name "$CLUSTER_NAME" `+      --cluster-type managedClusters `+      --name agent-sandbox `+      --extension-type Microsoft.AgentSandbox+    ```+3. Check the extension's provisioning state and installed version.++    ```powershell+    az k8s-extension show `+      --resource-group "$AKS_RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --cluster-name "$CLUSTER_NAME" `+      --cluster-type managedClusters `+      --name agent-sandbox `+      --query '{type:extensionType,state:provisioningState,version:currentVersion}'+    ```++    Continue only after `state` is `Succeeded` and `version` is `1.0.7` or later. A successful installation of an older version doesn't meet this requirement.++## Connect to the managed AKS cluster++Complete these steps after installing the extension and before running any workload commands.++1. Get credentials and select a context for the managed cluster.++    ```powershell+    $KUBE_CONTEXT = "$SUBSCRIPTION_ID-$SPACE_NAME"+    az aks get-credentials `+      --resource-group "$AKS_RESOURCE_GROUP" `+      --name "$CLUSTER_NAME" `+      --context "$KUBE_CONTEXT" `+      --overwrite-existing++    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {+      throw "Couldn't get cluster credentials. Check the cluster and your access before continuing."+    }++    kubectl config use-context "$KUBE_CONTEXT"+    ```++    Configure Kubernetes authentication to use your current Azure CLI sign-in instead of starting a separate device-code sign-in.++    ```powershell+    kubelogin convert-kubeconfig --login azurecli+    ```+2. Verify connectivity, wait for the controller, and check the Sandbox API and runtime.++    ```powershell+    kubectl cluster-info+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-sandbox-system rollout status `+      deployment/agent-sandbox-controller --timeout=5m+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl get crd sandboxes.agents.x-k8s.io `+      -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[?(@.served==true)].name}'+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl get runtimeclass virtualnode2 -o yaml+    ```++    Continue only after the controller rollout succeeds, the served API versions include `v1beta1`, and the `virtualnode2` RuntimeClass exists. If any check fails, resolve the installation or runtime configuration before creating a Sandbox.++## Run an isolated AI agent workload++1. Create a namespace for the example.++    ```powershell+    kubectl create namespace agent-demo+    ```+2. Create a file named `agent-sandbox.yaml` with the following manifest. Replace `<agent-container-image>` with your workload image. Adjust resource requests and limits for your workload.++    ```yaml+    apiVersion: agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1+    kind: Sandbox+    metadata:+      name: agent-demo+      namespace: agent-demo+    spec:+      podTemplate:+        metadata:+          labels:+            app: agent-demo+        spec:+          enableServiceLinks: false+          runtimeClassName: virtualnode2+          containers:+            - name: agent+              image: <agent-container-image>+              resources:+                requests:+                  cpu: 250m+                  memory: 512Mi+                limits:+                  cpu: "1"+                  memory: 1Gi+    ```+3. Apply the manifest.++    ```powershell+    kubectl apply -f agent-sandbox.yaml+    ```+4. Wait for the Sandbox and its backing pod to become Ready before you inspect the pod's placement.++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo wait --for=condition=Ready `+      sandbox/agent-demo --timeout=5m+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo wait --for=condition=Ready pod `+      --selector app=agent-demo --timeout=5m+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo get pods --selector app=agent-demo -o wide+    ```++    Check that `RUNTIME` is `virtualnode2` and `NODE` shows the assigned node.++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo get pods -l app=agent-demo `+      -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RUNTIME:.spec.runtimeClassName,NODE:.spec.nodeName+    ```++    Pod readiness alone doesn't prove that the workload completed initialization. Check your application's health endpoint or logs as appropriate.++## Configure a warm pool++This section is optional. Your standalone Sandbox is ready to use after you complete the preceding verification steps. Configure a warm pool if you need environments available before new agent sessions start.++A warm pool keeps Sandboxes running before an agent requests them, reducing the need to wait for a new environment to start. A `SandboxTemplate` defines the environment, a `SandboxWarmPool` maintains the available reserve, and a `SandboxClaim` requests a Sandbox from that pool. These resources must be in the same namespace.++This example uses the `agent-demo` namespace created earlier and maintains two available Sandboxes. Warm Sandboxes consume compute resources even when no agent is using them. Plan capacity for the reserve, claimed Sandboxes, and any standalone Sandboxes you created earlier. A warm pool doesn't require the Pod snapshot cluster extension.++### Check warm-pool API availability++1. Confirm that the extension installed all three resource definitions.++    ```powershell+    kubectl get crd `+      sandboxtemplates.extensions.agents.x-k8s.io `+      sandboxwarmpools.extensions.agents.x-k8s.io `+      sandboxclaims.extensions.agents.x-k8s.io+    ```+2. Verify the API version and claim field used by this example.++    ```powershell+    kubectl api-resources --api-group=extensions.agents.x-k8s.io+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl explain sandboxclaims.spec.warmPoolRef `+      --api-version=extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1+    ```++    Continue only if all three resources serve `extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` and the claim supports `warmPoolRef`. If a resource or field is missing, check the supported extension version before continuing. Don't install upstream controllers over the managed extension.++### Create a template and warm pool++1. Create `agent-warm-pool.yaml` from the following template. Replace `<agent-container-image>` with your long-running agent service image and adjust resource requests and limits for your workload.++    Important++    Before applying this template, add a container `readinessProbe` that checks whether your application finishes initialization and can accept work. The probe is application-specific and isn't included in this template. Without it, the pool can report an environment as Ready before the application is usable.++    ```yaml+    apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1+    kind: SandboxTemplate+    metadata:+      name: agent-template+      namespace: agent-demo+    spec:+      podTemplate:+        metadata:+          labels:+            app: agent-warm-pool+        spec:+          enableServiceLinks: false+          runtimeClassName: virtualnode2+          containers:+            - name: agent+              image: <agent-container-image>+              resources:+                requests:+                  cpu: 250m+                  memory: 512Mi+                limits:+                  cpu: "1"+                  memory: 1Gi+    ---+    apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1+    kind: SandboxWarmPool+    metadata:+      name: agent-warm-pool+      namespace: agent-demo+    spec:+      replicas: 2+      sandboxTemplateRef:+        name: agent-template+    ```+2. Apply the template and pool.++    ```powershell+    kubectl apply -f agent-warm-pool.yaml+    ```+3. Wait until two Sandboxes are Ready, then inspect the pool and its pods.++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo wait `+      --for=jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}'=2 `+      sandboxwarmpool/agent-warm-pool --timeout=10m+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo get sandboxwarmpool agent-warm-pool+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo get pods `+      --selector app=agent-warm-pool -o wide+    ```++    Confirm that the pool reports two ready sandboxes. The pod output shows their assigned nodes and current status. It doesn't verify the nodes' runtime configuration.++### Claim a Sandbox++Create a separate claim for each agent session. A claim takes ownership of an available Sandbox, and the pool creates a replacement to restore its reserve. The pool's replica count doesn't limit the total number of claimed Sandboxes.++1. Create `agent-sandbox-claim.yaml` with the following content.++    ```yaml+    apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1+    kind: SandboxClaim+    metadata:+      name: agent-session+      namespace: agent-demo+    spec:+      warmPoolRef:+        name: agent-warm-pool+    ```+2. Apply the claim and wait for it to become Ready.++    ```powershell+    kubectl apply -f agent-sandbox-claim.yaml+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo wait --for=condition=Ready `+      sandboxclaim/agent-session --timeout=10m+    ```+3. Get the assigned Sandbox name and inspect its status.++    ```powershell+    $CLAIMED_SANDBOX = kubectl -n agent-demo get `+      sandboxclaim agent-session -o jsonpath='{.status.sandbox.name}'+    ```++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo get sandbox "$CLAIMED_SANDBOX" -o yaml+    ```++    Use your application's health endpoint or logs to verify that the assigned environment is usable. To check that the pool replenishes its reserve, repeat the pool readiness check after the claim completes.+4. When the session ends, delete its claim and the owned Sandbox resources.++    ```powershell+    kubectl -n agent-demo delete sandboxclaim agent-session `+      --cascade=foreground --wait=true --timeout=5m+    ```++    Deleting the claim doesn't return the used Sandbox to the pool. The pool maintains its reserve with separate Sandboxes. Save any application data you need before deleting the claim.++### Change warm-pool capacity++To maintain three available Sandboxes instead of two, scale the pool:++```powershell+kubectl -n agent-demo scale sandboxwarmpool agent-warm-pool --replicas=3+```++```powershell+kubectl -n agent-demo wait `+  --for=jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}'=3 `+  sandboxwarmpool/agent-warm-pool --timeout=10m+```++Also update `spec.replicas` in `agent-warm-pool.yaml` so reapplying the file doesn't reset the capacity. Scaling the pool changes the unclaimed reserve, not Sandboxes already assigned to claims. Pool pods remain running and consume resources until you scale down or delete the pool.++## Restore a Sandbox from a pod snapshot++This section is optional. Use snapshot restore to resume captured workload state instead of starting a new environment. It doesn't require a warm pool.++You can install the [Pod snapshot cluster extension](pod-snapshot-cluster-extension) and Agent Sandbox in either order. The Pod snapshot manager detects the Sandbox API when it becomes available, including after the manager starts, without requiring a restart.++When following the Pod snapshot article, reuse this workload space and its deployment values. Don't create another workload space, new bindings, or a new runtime link. Install Pod snapshot directly on the managed AKS cluster identified earlier.++The serverless sandbox runtime supports only explicit restore. Specify the name of the snapshot to restore. Creating a Sandbox without restore intent starts a new workload normally.       "1",+          "2",+          "3"+        ]+      }+    ],     "restrictions": [-                    {-                        "type": "Zone",-                        "values": [- The sandbox is the isolation boundary for all containers and steps in a task run.++You're responsible for keeping secrets out of your images. Use a [`.dockerignore` file](https://docs.docker.com/build/concepts/context/#dockerignore-files) at the root of the Docker build context to exclude sensitive files such as private keys. `az acr build` applies ignore rules before uploading a local directory. For Git sources, Docker applies the rules during the image build.+ ## Image platforms  By default, Azure Container Registry tasks build images for the Linux OS and the AMD64 architecture. Specify the `--platform` tag to build Windows images or Linux images for other architectures. Specify the OS and optionally a supported architecture in *OS/architecture* format (for example, `--platform Linux/arm`). For ARM architectures, optionally specify a variant in *OS/architecture/variant* format (for example, `--platform Linux/arm64/v8`).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      @@ -1,5 +1,14 @@ # Container Network Insights Agent for AKS overview (Public Preview) - Azure Kubernetes Service | Microsoft Learn +Important++Container Network Insights Agent is being deprecated and won't be available after the end of November 2026. Plan to stop using the agent before then.++The agent is a public preview feature. It doesn't have a service-level agreement (SLA) and isn't recommended for production workloads. Preview features receive best-effort support. For more information, see:++- [AKS support policies](support-policies#preview-features-or-feature-flags)+- [AKS FAQ](faq)+ Container Network Insights Agent is an AI-powered diagnostic assistant that helps you identify and resolve networking issues in your Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters. Describe a problem in natural language, such as DNS failures, packet drops, unreachable services, or blocked traffic. The agent collects evidence from your cluster and returns a structured report with root cause analysis and remediation guidance.  Unlike tools that operate only at the Kubernetes layer, Container Network Insights Agent can also gather **host-level network statistics** through its Linux Networking plugin. The agent can inspect NIC ring buffers, kernel packet counters, SoftIRQ distribution, and socket buffer utilization across your cluster nodes. This surfaces low-level issues such as packet drops, network bottlenecks, and hardware-level saturation that are otherwise difficult to diagnose in a Kubernetes environment.

For details on what changed, see the following resources:+The command-level compatibility symlinks allow existing commands to invoke DNF5 without requiring the command name to change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     @@ -248,6 +248,27 @@ The `--gpu-instance-profile` feature remains available for configuration of your  All three single-strategy paths expose partitions as `nvidia.com/gpu` when configured on an NVIDIA GPU node pool. The resource name alone doesn't identify the partition size or whether AKS manages the plugin. +Important++[NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.20.1](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-container-toolkit/releases/tag/v1.20.1) and later won't start a container that sets `NVIDIA_MIG_CONFIG_DEVICES` or `NVIDIA_MIG_MONITOR_DEVICES` unless the container has the `SYS_ADMIN` capability. Self-managed device plugin and GPU feature discovery containers usually set one of these variables when they run with a MIG strategy. Without the capability, they fail with this error:++```output+invalid MIG capability request: cannot set NVIDIA_MIG_CONFIG_DEVICES or NVIDIA_MIG_MONITOR_DEVICES in a non-privileged container+```++The NVIDIA device plugin Helm chart adds `SYS_ADMIN` for you, unless you override `securityContext` in your values. If you override it, or you deploy your own manifest, add the capability yourself. Kubernetes doesn't allow `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` on a container that has `SYS_ADMIN`, so remove that setting or set it to `true`. You don't need `privileged: true`:++```yaml+securityContext:+  allowPrivilegeEscalation: true+  capabilities:+    add: ["SYS_ADMIN"]+```++For more information, see [Configure a security context for a pod or container](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/).++If AKS manages the device plugin for you, there's nothing to change. The managed plugin runs as a systemd service on the node, so this check doesn't apply to it.+ ### Validate the MIG profiles configuration  - Supply exactly one profile value to `--gpu-mig-profiles` for `Single`, not repeated entries to specify a partition count.
